chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon them), who said:

When a man marries off his daughter-in-law (his son's daughter), it is valid upon his son, and for the son also to marry her off. So I said, 'If her father desires a man and her grandfather desires a man?' He said: 'The grandfather is more entitled to her marriage.'
ai.seo_question: Who has the right to arrange the marriage of a granddaughter if the father and grandfather disagree?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration to clarify the hierarchy of *wilayah* (guardianship) in marriage, specifically addressing the potential conflict between a father and a paternal grandfather. While the father generally holds primary authority, this hadith establishes that the grandfather’s right takes precedence if he wishes to marry her to a different suitor, reflecting the Shia juristic view of the grandfather as the next tier of guardian after the father.
